documents.doc-cz-uoou-2026-08-26-uoou-05841-26-3: The Czech Office for Personal Data Protection stated that the Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office sent the appeal and the case file on 12 August 2026, but they were not received by the Office until 17 August 2026. According to the Office, the fifteen-day period under Section 16(3) of the Freedom of Information Act therefore runs from that delivery and expires on 1 September 2026. The Office also stated that no procedural act had yet been taken in the appeal proceedings and that the separate submission of 14 July 2026, supplemented on 12 August 2026, would be handled by the competent department in a separate letter.
documents.doc-cz-ks-ost-2026-08-26-st-82-2026-15-t: The Ostrava Regional Court confirmed that on 24 August 2026 it received a complaint concerning the conduct of proceedings before the Ostrava District Court in case 15 T 11/2025. Because the chair of the Ostrava District Court is competent to deal with the complaint, the Regional Court forwarded it to her on 26 August 2026.
documents.doc-cz-szu-2026-08-25-szu-10724-2026: The National Institute of Public Health responded to the information request concerning transport, storage and handover of human blood samples. It stated that pre-analytical handling and transport are the responsibility of the healthcare provider sending the sample, referred to its laboratory sampling manual, and stated that since 1 January 2021 it has recorded no degradation, refusal or challenge of a blood sample because of transport conditions.
documents.doc-cz-szu-2026-08-26-szu-10724-2026-roz: The National Institute of Public Health issued a decision partially refusing the information request under Section 11b of the Czech Freedom of Information Act. It refused information concerning methodologies, temperature ranges, transport without a validated box, high-temperature transport conditions, temperature monitoring and generally applicable validation requirements, stating that these matters fall within the competence of the healthcare providers sending samples. The decision may be appealed within 15 days to the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection through the Institute.
documents.doc-cz-msz-pha-2026-08-27-3-kzn-974-2026: The Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office completed supervisory review of the Prague 4 District Public Prosecutor’s Office in file 1 ZN 320/2026. It found no error requiring corrective action, dismissed the supervisory submission as unfounded and stated that the matter was finally disposed of at that level. It also advised that further submissions of identical content would no longer be reviewed or acknowledged.

The Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office completed supervisory review of the Prague 7 District Public Prosecutor’s Office in file ZN 87/2026. The review concerned the part of the submission relating to officials of the Ministry of the Interior. The Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office concluded that the materials did not sufficiently particularise facts indicating an offence under Sections 329 or 330 of the Criminal Code or another criminal offence, dismissed the supervisory submission as unfounded and stated that the matter was finally disposed of at that level. It also advised that further submissions of identical content would no longer be reviewed or acknowledged.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-08-28-8-ad-9-2026-85: The Prague Municipal Court rejected the intervention action against the Ministry of Health under Section 46(1)(a) of the Code of Administrative Justice, finding that the challenged classification of medicinal cannabis as a ‘highly addictive substance’ was not an individualised intervention against the claimant but part of the general statutory and regulatory framework. No party was awarded costs. After the order becomes final, the claimant is to receive a refund of the full CZK 2,000 court fee because the action was rejected before the first hearing; the Court requested bank details within 10 days. A cassation complaint may be filed within two weeks of service.
documents.doc-cz-mk-2026-08-31-mk-53547-2026-socns: The Czech Ministry of Culture discontinued the proceeding on the preparatory committee’s request for a new proceeding and a new decision concerning registration of the Cannabis Church under Section 101(b) of the Administrative Procedure Code. It accepted that the original registration request had been finally refused, but concluded that the new legal, factual, evidentiary and doctrinal circumstances did not justify a favourable new decision. The Ministry treated changes in cannabis law, THC/THCA forensic issues, EU-law arguments and the legal regime of cannabis religious objects as irrelevant to registration, regarded the more detailed explanation of the Church’s teaching as not constituting a new fact, and again concluded that the Cannabis Church did not satisfy the statutory definition of a church and religious society. A remonstrance may be filed within 15 days of service; it has no suspensive effect.
documents.doc-cz-mk-2026-08-31-mk-53559-2026-socns: The Czech Ministry of Culture answered questions raised in submissions of 26 June and 7 July 2026 and later supplements concerning the procedural status and registration of the Cannabis Church. It confirmed that the original registration proceeding had been finally concluded by the 2019 refusal, that the preparatory committee and its representative were and remain recorded as parties, and referred to the parallel order MK 53547/2026 SOCNS. The Ministry stated that it lacked competence to assess THC/THCA forensic methodology, the European Commission position or Danish materials, and treated the EU-law and preliminary-reference issues as irrelevant to the registration proceeding. It also stated that it had assessed the submissions according to their substance, good-administration principles, religious neutrality and protection of religious pluralism, and offered a possible personal meeting on further merits-related questions.
documents.doc-cz-msz-pha-2026-09-01-3-kzn-974-2026: The Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor's Office re-examined the relevant part of Dušan Dvořák's filing of 27 May 2026 and follow-up filings of 14, 15 and 19 July 2026 after the Brno Municipal Public Prosecutor's Office returned the transferred part under reference 3 ZN 140/2026-3. The Prague office concluded that the filings, insofar as they concerned persons serving or formerly serving at the Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office, did not contain concrete facts reasonably indicating an offence under Sections 329, 330 or another provision of the Criminal Code. It therefore filed the submissions without further action under Section 16a of the Public Prosecutor's Office Act and treated them as disposed of. The notice expressly states that the manner of disposal may be submitted for review under Section 16a(7) to the Prague High Public Prosecutor's Office.
documents.doc-cz-mz-2026-09-01-mzdr-21970-2026-3-m: The Czech Ministry of Health answered ten freedom-of-information questions submitted by Ganja For All Animals, z.s. about the collection, storage and transport of blood samples, blood and blood components. It cited the applicable legislation, the ČSN EN ISO 15189:2023 standard and professional guidance, and described storage temperatures, validation of transport boxes and vehicles, and transport monitoring. At the same time, the Ministry stated that it held neither the requested record and protocol templates nor inspection findings, methodological positions or records of temperature or time deviations since 1 January 2021, and refused those parts of the request. It identified the State Institute for Drug Control as the supervisory authority for blood banks, blood establishments and healthcare providers.

documents.doc-cz-nss-2026-09-04-6-as-207-2026-13: The Supreme Administrative Court confirmed receipt on 2 September 2026 of the cassation complaint against Prague Municipal Court order 15 A 44/2026-43 and requested a completed statement of personal, property and income circumstances within one week of service so it can decide the requests for exemption from court fees and appointment of counsel
documents.doc-cz-gibs-2026-09-08-gi-3794-4-cj-2026: The General Inspection of Security Forces stated on 8 September 2026, under ref. GI-3794-4/ČJ-2026-840502-P, that the filings delivered on 15 and 24 August 2026 concerning review of 2009-2019 proceedings and internal review of police procedures for determining THC in cannabis had been forwarded, according to subject-matter and territorial competence, to the Police Presidium of the Czech Republic for further measures. The Inspection also stated that it lacked authority to assess the challenged Police procedures or the factual and legal questions concerning evidence, and expressly treated the matter as disposed of on its side.
documents.doc-cz-msp-2026-09-08-msp-19-2026-odka-r: The Minister of Justice treated the submissions delivered on 12 July, 15 July, 10 August and 25 August 2026 as a request for measures against inactivity under Section 80(2) of the Administrative Procedure Code. He found the request unfounded, declined to take an inactivity measure and stated that the filing of 12 July 2026 was disposed of by this letter. He also stated that a settlement cannot be concluded in the administrative action and that further filings without new material facts may be placed on file without further written notice.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-09-09-8-ad-9-2026-89: On 9 September 2026, under ref. 8 Ad 9/2026-89, the Prague Municipal Court asked the claimant to provide a bank account number so that the court fee could be refunded pursuant to operative part III of the order of 28 August 2026, ref. 8 Ad 9/2026-85. The letter is an administrative follow-up implementing the already ordered refund; it does not itself decide the merits of the intervention action or record a new remedy.
documents.doc-cz-os-pro-2026-09-14-15-nt-3104-2026: On 14 September 2026, under ref. 15 Nt 3104/2026, the Prostějov District Court informed Dušan Dvořák that this file will be used to hear his application to reopen the proceedings previously conducted under file 2 T 104/2010. The letter is a procedural clarification identifying the reopening case; it does not itself grant reopening, decide the merits, create a new remedy or start a separate new timer.
documents.doc-cz-os-pro-2026-09-14-15-nt-3106-2026: On 14 September 2026, under ref. 15 Nt 3106/2026, the Prostějov District Court informed Dušan Dvořák that this file will be used to hear the application to reopen proceedings previously conducted under file 2 T 65/2011. The Court also stated that, in the original case, the public prosecutor withdrew the indictment and the criminal proceedings were subsequently discontinued. The letter is a procedural clarification; it does not itself grant reopening, decide the merits, create a new remedy or start a separate new timer.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-09-07-os-osz-pro-procesni: On 7 September 2026, Dušan Dvořák asked the Prostějov District Court and District Public Prosecutor’s Office for a precise procedural explanation of which original criminal case would be heard under files 15 Nt 3104/2026 and 15 Nt 3106/2026.
documents.doc-cz-ekk-2026-09-11-msp-cia-thc-dohled: On 11 September 2026, the Educational Cannabis Clinic submitted a filing to the Ministry of Justice and the Czech Accreditation Institute seeking review of forensic and laboratory practice in cannabis testing and quantitative THC determination, including sampling, homogenisation, THC/THCA, decarboxylation, validation, measurement uncertainty and accreditation scope.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-09-13-os-osz-pro-doplneni: A filing dated 13 September 2026 supplemented the Prostějov renewal proceedings 15 Nt 3104/2026 and 15 Nt 3106/2026 and related public-prosecution files, referring to the new 11 September Ministry/Accreditation filing and the 13 September closing communication to the Supreme Public Prosecutor and Czech Television.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-09-13-ks-ksz-vsz-doplneni: A filing dated 13 September 2026 supplemented Brno Regional Court complaint proceedings 9 To 315/2026 and 9 To 316/2026 and related supervision/review branches before the Olomouc High and Brno Regional Public Prosecutor’s Offices.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-09-13-nsz-ct-zaverecne-sd: The 13 September 2026 closing communication followed the pre-action demand to the Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office and the continuing complaint to Czech Television and its Council; it identified the 11 September article and the Ministry/Accreditation filing as new records.
documents.doc-cz-mv-2026-09-14-mv-139593-3-tp-2026: On 14 September 2026 the Ministry of the Interior dismissed the appeal dated 24 August 2026 and confirmed the Moravian-Silesian Regional Police decision of 20 August 2026, ref. KRPT-203594-8/ČJ-2026-0700KR, concerning partial refusal of an information request. The decision states that no further administrative appeal is available.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-09-14-9-ad-12-2026-7: On 14 September 2026 the Prague Municipal Court rejected the second identical intervention action in case 9 Ad 12/2026 because an earlier identical action filed on 31 August 2026 remains pending as 15 Ad 14/2026. The rejection of 9 Ad 12/2026 therefore does not terminate the earlier 15 Ad 14/2026 proceeding. The order allows a cassation complaint within two weeks of service; the service date is not recorded here.
documents.doc-cz-vsz-olo-2026-09-15-3-vzn-239-2026: On 15 September 2026 the Olomouc High Public Prosecutor’s Office explained how it handled submissions dated 15 and 24 August and 2, 3 and 13 September. It noted or had forwarded several filings and stated that supervision over district public prosecutor’s offices belongs to the directly superior regional offices; the 13 September filing was therefore noted without further measure at the High Office.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-09-16-os-ks-brno-predzase: The 16 September 2026 joint evidentiary and procedural supplement was addressed to the Prostějov District Court in files 15 Nt 3104/2026 and 15 Nt 3106/2026 and to the Brno Regional Court in files 9 To 315/2026 and 9 To 316/2026, following the Prostějov court clarifications of 14 September.
documents.doc-cz-os-pha4-2026-09-16-10-c-69-2026-p: On 16 September 2026, in case 10 C 69/2026 (Mgr. Dušan Dvořák v Czech Television, protection of personality), the Prague 4 District Court summoned the claimant to the first hearing, scheduled for 24 November 2026 at 13:00 in courtroom 3.308. The document fixes a concrete hearing date; it does not decide the merits of the case. The previous elapsed-time timer for waiting on the next procedural step is therefore removed, while the court case itself remains active.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-09-22-15-ad-14-2026-1: On 22 September 2026, under ref. 15 Ad 14/2026-12, the Prague Municipal Court stated that the court fee paid in proceeding 8 Ad 9/2026 cannot be transferred to the separate fee obligation in proceeding 15 Ad 14/2026. The Court also stated that an instruction to refund the fee paid in 8 Ad 9/2026 had already been issued. The communication does not terminate proceeding 15 Ad 14/2026 and sets no new deadline.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-09-23-18-a-23-2026-18: On 23 September 2026, under ref. 18 A 23/2026-182, the Prague Municipal Court sent the claimant, for information, the defendant Ministry of Justice's statement concerning the action, dated 27 August 2026. The Court set a one-week period from service of the covering letter for any reply. It also stated that it treats the case as a priority matter, but not as an extraordinarily urgent one. The uploaded PDF contains the Court's covering letter only, not the defendant's attached statement. Because the date of service is not evidenced in the document, no specific calendar deadline is inferred.
documents.doc-cz-msp-2026-08-27-msp-19-2026-odka-r: On 27 August 2026, under ref. MSP-19/2026-ODKA-ROZ/26 in case 18 A 23/2026, the Ministry of Justice submitted its statement on the intervention action and related case material. The Ministry argues that the claimant lacks standing and that no intervention within the meaning of Section 82 of the Code of Administrative Justice occurred; it proposes dismissal of the action as inadmissible and, alternatively, rejection on the merits. This is the defendant authority's litigation position, not a court determination of the merits.
documents.doc-cz-ms-pha-2026-09-23-18-a-17-2026-18: On 23 September 2026, under ref. 18 A 17/2026-182, the Prague Municipal Court stated that it had received the claimant's motion to set a time limit for a procedural act. Independently of the motion dated 21 September 2026, the Court said it had planned and still planned to decide case 18 A 17/2026 in the coming weeks, within the thirty-day framework referred to in Section 174a(3) of Act No. 6/2002. It therefore was not at that point forwarding the case file to the Supreme Administrative Court. No specific calendar decision date is inferred from the document.
documents.doc-eu-euda-2026-09-25-exo-fhp-pd-26-d-1: EUDA responded substantively to the formal call to act under Article 265 TFEU. The Agency stated that, in its view, Articles 6(1)(f) and 15 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1322 do not impose a specific, unconditional and legally binding obligation to carry out the requested comparative assessment or harmonisation work. At the same time, EUDA acknowledged that differences in analytical methods, the treatment of THC and THCA, sample preparation and storage, and approaches to measurement uncertainty may affect analytical outcomes and comparability. It also stated that it does not maintain a systematic inventory of national THC determination methodologies, has not carried out a systematic comparative assessment of those methodologies, and has not decided to conduct or commission such work.

documents.doc-cz-ksz-brn-2026-09-16-1-kzt-475-2026: The Brno Regional Public Prosecutor’s Office dismissed the request for supervision of the Prostějov District Public Prosecutor’s Office as unfounded. It stated that a prosecutor need not provide an opinion on reopening before the public hearing and that legal advice on cannabis cultivation falls outside the prosecution service’s remit. It nevertheless accepted that future submissions cannot be rejected indiscriminately, limiting that approach to repeated submissions containing no new facts. The notice addresses the filing of 10 July 2026 and supplements through 13 September 2026.
documents.doc-cz-vs-pha-2026-09-14-3-cmo-24-2026-2: The Prague High Court quashed the Prague Municipal Court’s order of 4 March 2026, reference 3 Cm 2/2026-19, refusing the Educational Cannabis Clinic’s applications for court-fee exemption and appointed counsel. It held that district courts have subject-matter jurisdiction over the claim for a reply against FTV Prima and ordered transfer to Prague 10 District Court once the order becomes final. It classified the claim as a statutory right of reply under broadcasting legislation. The order did not decide whether FTV Prima must publish the reply.
documents.doc-cz-msz-pha-2026-10-01-3-kzn-974-2026: The Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office reviewed the handling by the Prague 2 District Public Prosecutor’s Office in case 1 ZN 157/2026 and dismissed Dušan Dvořák’s supervisory request of 1 August 2026 as unfounded. It concluded that the transferred part of the 27 May 2026 filing concerning the Ministry of Justice did not contain sufficiently concrete facts reasonably indicating an offence under Sections 329, 330 or another provision of the Criminal Code. The Office treated notice 3 KZN 974/2026-114 of 1 October 2026 as the final disposition of the matter and stated that further submissions with the same content would not be reviewed.
documents.doc-cs-dd-2026-10-01-spolecne-doplneni-n: Urgent joint evidentiary supplement addressed to the Supreme Public Prosecutor’s Office, the Prague High Public Prosecutor’s Office and the Olomouc High Public Prosecutor’s Office. The filing relies on the Prague Municipal Public Prosecutor’s Office notice of 1 October 2026, ref. 3 KZN 974/2026-114, the Czech Defence Lawyers’ Union statement No. 3/2026 of 25 September 2026 and earlier forensic-methodology records. It asks the three offices to assess the linked chain of responsibility concerning sampling, homogenisation, THC/THCA, decarboxylation, measurement uncertainty and laboratory SOPs instead of fragmenting the issue into isolated branches.
documents.doc-cz-ksz-brn-2026-10-01-1-spr-338-2026: The Brno Regional Public Prosecutor’s Office disposed of Dušan Dvořák’s complaint about delays. It stated that the review in case 1 KZT 475/2026 had been completed on 16 September 2026 and the notice dispatched on 18 September, but due to an administrative error it was not delivered to his data box until 29 September 2026; the Office apologised. In case 1 KZN 1079/2026 it stated that the review period had been extended to 9 October 2026 and expected written notification within that extended period.
documents.doc-cz-dd-2026-10-01-os-pro-bezplatna-ob: On 1 October 2026, Dušan Dvořák asked the Prostějov District Court to grant him free defence under Section 33(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and to appoint defence counsel in both reopening proceedings, files 15 Nt 3104/2026 and 15 Nt 3106/2026.
